title: Luna-1: The Moon Landing
description: Apollo 11 and the race to the Moon.

questions.question: Which Apollo mission first landed humans on the Moon?
questions.explain: Apollo 11 landed on July 20, 1969.

questions.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.explain: Armstrong stepped onto the surface first, followed by Buzz Aldrin.

questions.question: Who was the second person to walk on the Moon?
questions.explain: Aldrin followed Armstrong out about 20 minutes later.

questions.question: Who piloted the command module and stayed in lunar orbit during Apollo 11?
questions.explain: Collins orbited the Moon alone while the other two landed.

questions.question: The Apollo 11 lunar module was named Eagle.
questions.explain: The command module was named Columbia.

questions.question: What year did Apollo 11 land on the Moon?
Which country's space program did the US race against during the Space Race?
questions.explain: The Cold War rivalry drove the US and USSR's space programs.

questions.question: What was Neil Armstrong's famous quote when stepping onto the Moon? Type the first word.
questions.explain: "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind."

questions.question: Which Moon region did Apollo 11 land in?
questions.explain: Mare Tranquillitatis, a flat volcanic plain.

questions.question: Apollo 11 was the first crewed mission to orbit the Moon.
questions.explain: Apollo 8 was first to orbit the Moon, in December 1968.

questions.question: What rocket launched the Apollo 11 mission?
questions.explain: The Saturn V remains the most powerful rocket ever flown successfully.

questions.question: How long did Armstrong and Aldrin stay on the lunar surface?
questions.explain: They spent roughly 21.5 hours on the surface, including about 2.5 hours outside the lander.

questions.question: The astronauts left an American flag on the Moon.
questions.explain: They also left a plaque reading "We came in peace for all mankind."

questions.question: Which US president challenged the nation to reach the Moon by the end of the decade?
questions.explain: Kennedy's 1961 speech set the goal for the 1960s.

questions.question: What was the name of the Apollo 11 command module?
questions.explain: Collins remained aboard Columbia in lunar orbit.

questions.question: Which Apollo mission suffered an oxygen tank explosion and had to abort its Moon landing?
questions.explain: The crew of Apollo 13 returned safely despite the failure.

questions.question: A total of twelve people have walked on the Moon.
questions.explain: All twelve were part of the US Apollo program, between 1969 and 1972.

questions.question: Which Apollo mission was the last to land humans on the Moon?
questions.explain: Apollo 17 landed in December 1972; Apollo 18 was cancelled.

questions.question: What agency ran the Apollo program?
questions.explain: NASA, the US space agency, founded in 1958.

questions.question: There is no wind on the Moon, so footprints left by astronauts can last millions of years.
questions.explain: With no atmosphere or weather, undisturbed footprints erode extremely slowly.
